target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with cancer and autoimmune disease; revenue so far from venture capital and government grants rather than customers
problem: Conventional mRNA therapies act in many cell types and cell therapies like CAR-T are slow, costly and limited to specialized centers; Kernal wants mRNA that is translated only inside chosen cell types, including in vivo CAR-T programming.
business_model: Therapeutics R&D company funded by venture rounds and grants, aiming at partnerships and drug approval
product_category: Cell-selective mRNA therapeutics (mRNA 2.0, in vivo CAR-T)

founders.name: Burak Yilmaz
education: M.S. (field and school not stated on YC page)
previous_startups: Sentegen / Sentebiolab (synthetic DNA and RNA company, still operating per company bio)

founders.name: Jeff Ozdemir
education: PhD Molecular Genetics, UT Southwestern Medical Center
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page. A Webrazzi article (2020-10-07) names a third founder Cafer Ozdemir, probably the same person; this is not confirmed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Selective mRNA translation and targeted LNP delivery were research-grade problems in 2020, requiring drug discovery, delivery chemistry and clinical development.

defensibility.rationale: Patents (company claims over 120 across the team's history) and a long clinical path make a platform hard to copy, though several mRNA delivery rivals work on the same goal.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying the selective translation approach; Amgen Ventures became an investor in 2022 and Lilly Gateway Labs admitted Kernal in October 2025.

market_need_then: In October 2020 the founders pitched mRNA candidates for cancer and Covid-19 with cheaper production than existing therapies (Webrazzi, 2020-10-07); the Covid-19 mRNA wave created investor attention for mRNA platforms.

branding.domain_note: Uses kernalbio.com, not an exact kernal.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; tagline 'Decoding the language of cells for selective medicines' and short tagline 'Code. Go.'

brand_strength.rationale: A scientific brand known mainly within biotech press; no source shows brand-driven growth. The spelling kernal is a misspelling of kernel and the site only uses 'kernal' as the core of its platform without explaining the name.

outcome_analysis: Kernal is a deep-tech mRNA company that raised a $25M Series A in 2022 led by Hummingbird with Amgen Ventures, then won an ARPA-H award of up to $48M in October 2025 for its in vivo CAR-T program KR-402 and joined Lilly Gateway Labs. Strengths are founders with pharma and academic credentials and a differentiated selective-translation platform; it is still pre-approval, so the outcome is open.
notes: Series A closing date conflicts: press in July 2022 versus a secondary source and CB Insights saying February 2022; July 2022 used. Fierce Biotech says the ARPA-H award is shared with three sub-awardees, so Kernal's own share may be smaller. One aggregator gives total funding about $35.8M, unverified. Founding year 2016 comes from a secondary profile; Webrazzi says R&D began in 2017. The 2020 Webrazzi article names no competitors, so the list is empty; current rivals named by aggregators (Moderna, Capstan, Orna, Strand) are undated and not used. Funding rounds before the 2022 Series A were not found.
